text.name: helpLine_cs_p1_intro_text
text.text: Seasonal Crop Stress adds soil moisture simulation to every field. Crops need water during key growth stages. If they don't get it, your harvest will be smaller. Irrigation systems let you take control of your field's water supply.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p1_start_text
text.text: Press Shift+M to open the moisture HUD and see all your fields at a glance. Fields shown in red need water urgently. Green fields are in good shape. Press Shift+C to open the Crop Consultant for detailed advice and field risk scores.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p2_how_text
text.text: Rain fills your soil and heat drains it. Every field tracks its own moisture level from 0% (bone dry) to 100% (saturated). The rate of drying depends on the weather, the season, and your soil type.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p2_soil_text
text.text: Sandy soil drains fast and needs frequent irrigation. Clay soil holds water longer but can become waterlogged. Loamy soil is in between and the easiest to manage. Your field's soil type is shown in the HUD and Crop Consultant.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p3_window_text
text.text: Every crop has a period during its growth cycle when it needs water the most. Wheat is most vulnerable in spring, corn suffers during summer heat waves, canola is sensitive in autumn. Low moisture during this window builds up stress on that field.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p3_yield_text
text.text: Accumulated stress reduces your harvest. A small amount of stress means a small yield loss. Severe drought can cut your harvest by up to 60%. The Crop Consultant shows your current yield risk per field so you can prioritise irrigation where it matters most.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p5_types_text
text.text: Three irrigation types are available in the build menu. Center Pivot covers a large circular area. Drip Line provides precise coverage along a field row. Water Pump powers your irrigation systems and must be placed near a water source first.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p5_schedule_text
text.text: Select an irrigation system and press Shift+I to open its schedule. Pick which days of the week to irrigate and set a daily start and end time. You can also press Irrigate Now in the dialog to water the covered fields immediately without waiting for the schedule.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p6_what_text
text.text: Press Shift+C to open the Crop Consultant. It shows your top 5 highest-risk fields ranked by moisture and stress level, along with a plain-language recommendation for the next 24 hours and a 3-day moisture forecast.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p6_act_text
text.text: Fields marked CRITICAL need irrigation today to prevent harvest loss. Fields marked WARNING should be irrigated within a day or two. Use the Open Irrigation Manager button inside the Consultant to quickly schedule water for the worst field.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p6_npc_text
text.text: Several optional mods extend the system. FS25_NPCFavor: Alex Chen appears as an Agronomist NPC — complete favors to unlock early drought warnings and specialist irrigation advice. FS25_SoilFertilizer: Soil pH and organic matter modify evapotranspiration per field. FS25_UsedPlus: Irrigation running costs and equipment wear are tracked. CoursePlay: Active vehicle counts appear in stress alerts. AutoDrive: Water destination hints appear in critical alerts. Precision Farming DLC: Soil moisture is shown in the PF map overlay.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s1_gen_text
text.text: Open the in-game settings (ESC → Settings → Seasonal Crop Stress). Use Enable Mod to switch the entire system on or off without removing your irrigation infrastructure. The Difficulty setting controls how quickly crops accumulate drought stress — Easy is forgiving, Hard pushes you to irrigate proactively.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s1_evap_text
text.text: Evapotranspiration controls how quickly soil dries out between rain events. Slow means fields hold moisture well and rain goes a long way. Fast means fields can dry out within a game-day during hot weather — active irrigation management becomes essential.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s2_yield_text
text.text: Max Yield Loss caps the percentage of harvest that drought stress can reduce. At the default 60%, a fully stressed field still yields 40% of normal. Critical Threshold is the moisture level below which stress begins to accumulate — raise it to make crops more drought-sensitive, lower it for more tolerance.

text.name: helpLine_cs_s2_alerts_text
text.text: Irrigation Costs charges an hourly fee for running irrigation systems, adding a financial management layer. Disable this for a simpler experience. Alerts Enabled shows warning notifications when fields need water. Alert Cooldown sets the minimum in-game hours before the same field triggers another alert, preventing notification spam.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_hud_text
text.text: Press Shift+M to toggle the moisture HUD. It lists every field with its moisture level, crop type, and stress status. A 5-day forecast shows whether moisture is rising or falling so you can plan ahead. You can also drag the panel to any position on screen by clicking and releasing.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_reading_text
text.text: Each row shows: field number (F1), crop name (Wheat), current growth stage (Stage 3), a colour-coded moisture bar, and the moisture percentage. If the row ends with an exclamation mark (!), that field is already building drought stress and yield loss has begun — irrigate it now. Only crops that can suffer drought stress appear in the list.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_status_text
text.text: Green means your field is healthy and no action is needed. Yellow is a warning: moisture is dropping and irrigation is advisable soon. Red is critical: the crop is under drought stress and yield loss is already building — irrigate immediately.

text.name: helpLine_cs_p4_keys_text
text.text: Shift+M toggles the moisture HUD on or off. Shift+I opens the Irrigation Manager for a selected system. Shift+C opens the Crop Consultant with a field risk summary and personalised recommendations.

text.name: helpLine_cs_t2_sandy_text
text.text: Sandy soil dries out twice as fast as loamy soil. If you farm a mix of soil types, place irrigation on sandy fields first. A centre pivot covering a large sandy area is often a better investment than a drip line on a small clay field that holds moisture naturally.

text.name: helpLine_cs_t2_forecast_text
text.text: The 5-day forecast in the HUD shows whether moisture is trending up or down. If rain is forecast within a day or two and your fields are only in the warning range, wait for the rain — you will save money and wear on your equipment. Act early when the forecast shows several dry days ahead during a critical growth window.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i1_about_text
text.text: Created by TisonK. Adds realistic soil moisture simulation, seasonal crop stress accumulation, and irrigation infrastructure management to Farming Simulator 25. Designed to make crop management more strategic — every field, every season, every decision counts.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i1_community_text
text.text: Find this mod on Github and KingMods. For questions, bug reports, and updates please visit the github repository.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i2_npc_text
text.text: With FS25_NPCFavor installed, Alex Chen appears as an Agronomist NPC on your farm. Completing favors for Alex builds your relationship and unlocks early drought warnings and specialist irrigation advice. With FS25_SoilFertilizer, each field's soil pH and organic matter content adjusts evapotranspiration — fields with poor soil health dry out faster, making good soil management worthwhile alongside irrigation.

text.name: helpLine_cs_i2_vehicle_text
text.text: When CoursePlay is active, the number of autonomous vehicles working a stressed field is shown in that field's alert. When AutoDrive is detected, critical drought alerts include available water destination counts and a suggestion to set up a hauling route. With FS25_UsedPlus, hourly irrigation running costs are charged and equipment wear accumulates realistically. If the Precision Farming DLC is active, soil moisture data is shown directly in the PF soil map overlay.

text.name: helpLine_cs_t3_sprayer_text
text.text: Standard vehicle-based sprayers can be used as a manual alternative to permanent irrigation systems. If you fill a sprayer with WATER, any area you spray will receive an immediate moisture boost. This is useful for small fields or as a temporary measure until you can afford a centre pivot or drip line.

text.name: cs_rf_pda_select_field
text.text: Select a field in the table for details.

text.name: rf_pda_side_info_soil
text.text:
Soil Fertilizer
This table lists every field you own. One row = one field.
Columns: Field #, Area, N/P/K (% of a healthy target), Status (Good / Fair / Poor), Fertilizer need (short cue for what still looks short).
Click a row. Treatment (below) is the plan for that field: - PRODUCT = what to buy (first is preferred; "or ..." is an alternate) - RATE = amount per area / TOTAL = amount for this field - Selected names the field; Next (under it) says what to do first
How to apply: dry goods (urea, MAP, potash, lime) go through a fertilizer spreader; liquids go in a sprayer tank. If pH and nutrients both show, fix lime or gypsum first so nutrients can work. Weed, pest, or disease lines mean spray (or weed mechanically) before you expect a full crop.
Start with the weakest Status, open Treatment, follow Next, then the rest of the list.

text.name: rf_pda_side_info_crop_stress
text.text:
Crop Stress
This screen is the Crop Stress desk. Each line is one field you own.
The table shows Field, Crop, Moisture, Stress, Irrigated, and Status. Moisture is how wet the soil is. Stress is how hard the crop is fighting dry spells. Irrigated says a system can reach this field. Status is Healthy, Warning, or Critical.
Click a row. Field Detail on the left coaches that field and Next says the first job. AGRONOMIST on the right lists the top risk fields. PIVOT below drives the irrigation system for the selected field.
On PIVOT, grey remotes are locked until the step before them is done. Open the door, then power, then the rest. An empty seat means no pivot covers this field.
Start with Critical Status, follow Next, then work up the list.
Irrigator kit (shop): pump + Rainstar + pull bar. Unfold, pull the gun out, turn it on over a field.

text.name: cs_rf_pda_next_no_coverage

text.text: Warning: only 10 m of hose remain on the reel.

text.text: Warning: only 30 m of hose remain on the reel.

text.text: Maximum hose length of 220 m reached.

text.name: warning_RAINSTAR_HOSE_NOT_EXTENDED
text.text: The sprinkler cart is already at the reel.

text.name: warning_RAINSTAR_PUMP_NOT_CONNECTED
text.text: Connect the motor pump to the Rainstar first.

text.name: warning_RAINSTAR_PUMP_NOT_RUNNING

text.name: warning_RAINSTAR_SELECT_WORKMODE
text.text: Select work mode before starting hose retraction.

text.name: scs_playkit_day_teach
text.text: Tow the reel out on the pull bar, park the cart at the far end, then walk to the pump and start it. Connect the hose at the pump, switch the reel on, and the gun waters as it reels back in. Stop the pump and hitch the bar again to pack up.

text.name: cs_rainstar_needs_pump
text.text: Connect the supply hose from the pump and start the pump. This reel runs on pump pressure, not a tractor.

text.name: cs_playkit_pump_power_teach
text.text: The pump is the power. Hitch the reel only to tow it: to spray, run the hose from the pump, start the pump, then switch the reel on. Stop the pump or pull the hose and the spray stops.
